$comment: The Coliseum: one handcrafted, bounded world, roughly 1.5km across, from GDD section 3.1. Not five separate levels and not procedurally assembled - Plains/Forest is the permanent spawn at the centre and the four others ring it on the diagonals at equal distance, with connective forest between. Distances are in Unreal units (1uu = 1cm), kept as canon so the PC and mobile builds describe the same space; the mobile renderer scales them. Distance from spawn is the difficulty axis - nothing gates on player level, because the world is meant to create its own reason to leave the centre.

travelSeconds.$comment: Spawn to biome edge. Measured in the PC blockout, not a target.

biomes.name: Plains / Forest
biomes.mood: Open, bright, unthreatening. Where you always start and always return.

biomes.name: Snowy Mountain
biomes.mood: Cold, vertical, lit from within. The sole source of Glacite.

biomes.name: Desert
biomes.mood: Exposed. Nowhere to hide, and visible from far off.

biomes.name: Wetland
biomes.mood: Low visibility, slow going. Cover in every direction.

biomes.name: Abandoned Data-Center
biomes.mood: Neon light and coolant fog. Still running, with growth creeping through it. The sole source of Umbrel.

$scale_comment: Canon distances are Unreal units (1uu = 1cm) so the PC and mobile builds describe the same space. The mobile renderer divides by this to get screen units. At 12, the gauntlet's base 600uu pull reads as a 50px radius - comfortable for a thumb - and spawn to biome edge comes out at roughly 32 seconds on foot, which is canon's measured 30-35.
$density_comment: Node counts are set from the loop, not from taste: a walking player sweeps a corridor twice the pull radius wide, so counts are chosen to yield roughly one pickup every four or five seconds on foot. That makes a 30-second biome crossing worth about six materials and fills the 60-unit cap over a long expedition rather than an ordinary walk. Plains/Forest carries a little more because it holds six materials to the others' three.
$terrain_comment: Each region already stated a mechanical identity in its own mood line and none of it existed - the biomes were a palette and a loot table, so the Wetland with "cover in every direction" played identically to the Desert with "nowhere to hide". terrain makes those lines true. moveScale multiplies walking speed; concealment multiplies how far enemies notice the player while they are standing here, so below 1 is cover and above 1 is exposure; sight multiplies how far the player senses; fog is a 0..1 haze drawn in the palette fog colour. Values blend toward neutral across the disc edge, so crossing a border is a gradient rather than a step.
